macro_blurb: US tech sentiment is leading the tape after a strong Dell earnings print framed an "AI stocks" catalyst week, while software names just closed their best month since 2001 as fears of a so-called "SaaSpocalypse" faded. Energy is moving the other way, with Brent crude posting its biggest monthly loss in six years as traders price in a potential US-Iran nuclear deal, though Trump ended the latest Iran meeting without a final determination, keeping the oil thesis unresolved. In European corporate news, private credit firm Castlelake is exploring a bid for easyJet, putting the UK low-cost airline space in focus. On the policy side, the IRS released 2027 HSA contribution limits, a minor US household-finance data point.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a US deep-value-and-momentum book with almost no defensive ballast. All 10 picks are US-listed, average Value sits at the 83rd percentile and Momentum at the 84th, while Quality lags at 59 — this is a cheap, moving, middling-quality basket, not a compounders list. Healthcare dominates with 3 of 10 names (CNC, DVA, BIIB), Consumer Cyclical adds 2 (BBY, DECK), and the composite range is tight at 71.3–82.9, so conviction is broad rather than concentrated in a single name. Leadership belongs to MO at 82.9, carried by an 86th-percentile Momentum read and an 86th-percentile Yield — a Consumer Defensive top pick is itself a tell about where the screen is finding paid-to-wait setups.

The thread worth pulling is healthcare-on-sale-with-a-tape: CNC (100th percentile Value, 23.3% FCF yield, +33.6% 3M), DVA (+26.2% 3M, debt/equity 1,261) and BIIB all surface as cheap names the market has started to re-rate despite poor quality optics — CNC's ROE is -26%, DVA's leverage is extreme, BIIB carries pipeline overhang. Separately, APA (13.1% FCF yield, 100th percentile Momentum) sits awkwardly against a macro where Brent just posted its worst month in six years on a possible US-Iran deal; the screen likes the cash flow, the tape is fighting it.

The outlier is EG — 97th-percentile Value, 0.84x book, but the only pick with negative 3-month return (-4.6%) and sub-median Momentum, a reminder that one name here is cheap because it's been sold. The conspicuous absence is Technology: zero picks despite software closing its best month since 2001 and Dell framing an AI catalyst week — this screen is structurally on the other side of the leading tape, alongside missing Utilities and Real Estate. Two things to watch over the next fortnight: any final US-Iran determination, which directly threatens APA and indirectly MO's relative-yield appeal, and continued AI/SaaS leadership, which would keep this value book underperforming the index it isn't in.
